summary:
Prince Edward Island stands under the national framework of Canada. The province's own instruments govern gender-marker changes on provincial documents, driver's licence markers, and family law.

In 2016 the MacLauchlan government tabled a bill amending the Vital Statistics Act so that an Islander can change the gender recorded on official provincial documents by declaring the gender they identify with and providing a letter from a doctor. Sex-reassignment surgery ceased to be required, and the province's gender-marker change has operated without a surgery requirement since that amendment.

The change is open only to a person born on Prince Edward Island who has lived in the province for at least three months and is not in the lawful custody of another person. A visitor cannot obtain a Prince Edward Island gender-marker change during a stay, so the provincial identification presented on arrival carries the marker set before travel.

Driver's licence markers became a separate provincial choice on 4 December 2018, when Access PEI locations began offering "gender not listed", shown on the licence as X, and "prefer not to say", shown as a blank field, alongside male and female. The government release of 30 November 2018 stated that Prince Edward Island was the first jurisdiction in Canada to offer the blank option, quoting Transportation, Infrastructure and Energy Minister Paula Biggar and the group PEERS Alliance. Provincial photo ID can therefore carry an X or a blank gender marker.

Reaction to the 2016 bill came from Pride P.E.I. board member Jesse Macmillan, who welcomed the removal of the surgery requirement, noting that surgery is expensive and the closest provider was in Montreal, and who called for a future third gender category, saying many of his friends in Charlottetown identify outside the binary. A linked item on the same article page reported that Health PEI would cover the costs of three surgeries for transgender patients.

The Statistics Canada release of 30 March 2026 on police-reported hate crime for 2024 gives no Prince Edward Island rate and no incident count for the province, and documents no pattern deviating for Prince Edward Island. This record therefore contains no province-specific hate-crime measurement to weigh against the marker and identification rules above.
tangentialFactors:
On one measure Prince Edward Island sits ahead of other Canadian jurisdictions: the release of 30 November 2018 described the province as the first in Canada to offer a blank "prefer not to say" gender field on a driver's licence, with the X marker available from 4 December 2018 at Access PEI locations.

Provincial family law moved early as well. Prince Edward Island allowed joint adoption in 2009, before the remaining provinces and territories completed the change, the last of which did so in 2011.

The removal of the surgery requirement in 2016 was welcomed on cost grounds, since surgery is expensive and the nearest provider identified in the reporting was in Montreal, in another province. Care of this kind has therefore historically required travel off the island.
localsOnly:
An adult may apply for a change of gender designation if born on Prince Edward Island, resident in the province for at least three months, and not in the lawful custody of another person.

A legal custodian may apply for a minor under 18 who was born on Prince Edward Island and has lived in the province for at least three months. The application needs the written consent of any other custodian or parent and the written consent of the child if the child is aged 12 or older.

The application requires completed forms including a physician statement and a written statement by the applicant, with the signature arranged before a commissioner of oaths at Vital Statistics. The regime runs without a surgery requirement and with physician attestation.

Health PEI would cover the costs of three surgeries for transgender patients, according to a linked item on the CBC News article page of 18 April 2016. The scope, eligibility and current status of that coverage are not documented in this record.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Prince Edward Island-specific hate-crime rate or incident count is published in the Statistics Canada release of 30 March 2026. The only comparator in that release is national: 4,882 police-reported hate crimes in 2024, up 1% on 2023, at a rate of 12.1 per 100,000 population, down 2% in 2024 and up 142% since 2018, with eight provinces recording stable or declining rates. Whether Prince Edward Island sits above or below that national rate is unresolved.

Egale Canada's 2024 analysis of police-reported hate-crime data covers sexual-orientation and gender-identity motivations nationally and supplies no Prince Edward Island breakdown, so it cannot be used to characterise province-level risk.

Whether the Vital Statistics Act permits a non-binary or third gender designation on a Prince Edward Island birth certificate is not sourced here. The X and blank markers are documented for driver's licences only, effective 4 December 2018, and the 2016 call by Pride P.E.I. for a third gender category has no documented outcome in this inventory.

No trans-specific violence incident, human rights complaint, or enforcement record for Prince Edward Island appears in this inventory, and no undated prevalence claim about such harm can be made from it. The most recent Prince Edward Island-specific official material in this record is the government information page captured 1 July 2022; no later province-specific instance is documented.

No Prince Edward Island-specific survey of public attitudes toward transgender residents is sourced. The 2020 Privy Council Office poll cited in the inventory, in which 87.6% of respondents said they would be comfortable with a transgender neighbour, is national in scope and does not measure opinion on the island.
